Subject: BioFirm: DPA + SCCs — initial redlines and asks

Team —

We had a productive call with BioFirm (Sara and Michael) this morning. They sent over their DPA redlines and an updated Order Form that references additional data export controls. Key asks from them:

- Confirm whether Redwood will accept the controller/processor mapping they proposed (they are insisting we sign as "Processor").
- Agreement to their expanded audit and deletion language (they want 90-day retention default and stronger deletion warranty).
- Inclusion of EU SCCs + a Transfer Impact Addendum and a named subprocessor list.

I attached their files (BioFirm_DPA_proposed_redlines.docx, BioFirm_OrderForm_marked.pdf).

Timeline: they want final DPA + executed Order Form before the renewal window on Oct 15.

Can legal weigh in on the high-risk items below and suggest RWI-friendly redlines we can take to counsel? Also flag anything that should go to Product/Infra (e.g., KMS/retention controls).

High-risk items I noted:
- Broad audit rights + onsite audit clause.
- Deletion language that could require us to retrieve/return customer prompts that are embedded in model outputs (needs clarity).
- Unlimited liability carve-outs tied to data breaches.
- SCCs + TIA — need to confirm whether our hosting (US/UK regions) requires additional safeguards.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick sync.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop

Subject: Re: BioFirm: DPA + SCCs — initial redlines and asks

Thanks Lauren — good summary.

I drafted a quick internal checklist for LegalOps to cover before we send RWI's redline back to BioFirm / their external counsel:
1) Role mapping: confirm RWI is Processor and BioFirm is Controller (their redline already assumes Processor, but need to call out subprocessor chain).
2) SCCs: accept EEA-to-US/UK transfers via EU SCCs + add limited Transfer Impact Addendum language (technical safeguards) rather than broad contractual warranties.
3) Audit rights: push for remote, scoped audits for cause only; reject unconditional onsite audits.
4) Deletion/Return: clarify what "Customer Content" includes (prompts vs model snapshots); limit obligation to best-effort deletion of stored customer artifacts and attest via certificate.
5) Security measures: confirm KMS usage, encryption at rest/in transit, and role-based access logs documented.
6) Liability & indemnity: preserve our MSA caps; propose carve-outs only for gross negligence and willful misconduct.

Could someone from legal take the attached BioFirm redline and produce: (A) a tracked RWI redline, and (B) a 1-page summary of the proposed changes we can share with the customer? We should also identify any Product asks so we can commit to feasible timelines.

I will loop in external counsel once we have the RWI redline.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales — Enterprise, Redwood Inference

Subject: BioFirm — quick questions on role mapping and transfers

Hi Karthik / Lauren —

Thanks for the redline and notes. I represent BioFirm on this engagement. A couple of clarifying questions before we review RWI's proposed changes:

1) Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept the Processor role (BioFirm is the Controller)? Any language that suggests joint-controller will be difficult for my client.
2) BioFirm's security team requires explicit identification of the KMS scope for export controls and whether keys are customer-managed. Is that something Redwood supports at the Order Form level?
3) On SCCs / Transfer Impact: BioFirm believes the SaaS nature of the service requires supplementary safeguards (TIA). Would Redwood accept a short, joint TIA that references specific technical measures (encryption, access controls, limited geo-locations) rather than broader legal warranties?

If you can share RWI's redline this week, we can circle back quickly. We also have an external DocuSign for the Order Form that we'd prefer to use once redlines are agreed.

Best,
Emma Jackson
Senior Counsel — HC Law Partners
emma.jackson@hc-law.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 3 Oct 2025 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BioFirm — quick questions on role mapping and transfers

Emma —

Short answers to your questions:
1) Yes — Redwood will accept the Processor role. We'll mark that clearly in the DPA and MSA definitions; we cannot accept joint-controller status.
2) KMS: We offer both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) for account-level encryption. For BioFirm's use case we can document a customer-managed key option in the Order Form and the DPA.
3) Transfer Impact Addendum: we're willing to include a short TIA that references the SCCs and enumerates technical controls (encryption at rest/in transit, RBAC, logging, region constraints). We'll ask legal to avoid open-ended legal guarantees and keep the TIA focused on measurable safeguards.

I'm attaching RWI's proposed DPA redline (RWI_DPA_v3_redlines.docx) and a 1-page summary for BioFirm to review.

Goal: finalize redlines and exchange signatures via DocuSign by Oct 14 so billing/procurement can process renewal.

—Karthik

Attachments: RWI_DPA_v3_redlines.docx

Karthik —

Received RWI_DPA_v3_redlines.docx and the 1-pager. We reviewed with BioFirm's security counsel and made a handful of targeted edits — primarily tightening the definition of Customer Content, swapping onsite audit for remote-for-cause with agreed notice periods, and clarifying retention/deletion obligations (certificate of deletion acceptable). We also inserted a short Transfer Impact Addendum that references SCCs and lists the following safeguards: AES-256 encryption at rest, TLS1.3 in transit, key management options, RBAC with audit logs retention 12 months.

We can proceed on two tracks: (1) accept these redlines and exchange a DocuSign Order Form referencing the attached DPA; or (2) propose one more small revision to limitations of liability (BioFirm prefers a higher cap tied to fees). If you can confirm track (1) by EOD we will send DocuSign for signature.
